definitions.explanation: Originally, a samurai without a sword at the waist. Now used literally for being without weapons or figuratively for being unprepared or defenseless.
Figuratively, going into a situation without the tools, knowledge, or preparation needed. Entering a confrontation or negotiation at a disadvantage.

examples.japanese: {丸腰|まるごし}で{戦|たたか}う。
{犯人|はんにん}は{丸腰|まるごし}だった。
{武器|ぶき}を{持|も}った{相手|あいて}に{丸腰|まるごし}で{立|た}ち{向|む}かった。
examples.english: He stood up to an armed opponent while unarmed.

examples.japanese: {資料|しりょう}も{用意|ようい}せず{丸腰|まるごし}で{会議|かいぎ}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I went to the meeting unprepared, without any materials.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}の{場|ば}に{丸腰|まるごし}で{行|い}くわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't go to the negotiation table empty-handed.

examples.japanese: {丸腰|まるごし}で{面接|めんせつ}に{臨|のぞ}んだが、{意外|いがい}と{上手|うま}くいった。
examples.english: I went into the interview unprepared, but it went surprisingly well.

notes:
From {丸|まる} (bare/completely) + {腰|こし} (waist/hip). In the samurai era, swords were worn at the waist, so {丸腰|まるごし} meant a bare waist — no sword. Used as a no-adjective modifier ({丸腰|まるごし}の).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸腰|まるごし}で{挑|いど}む: to take on a challenge unarmed/unprepared
- {丸腰|まるごし}の{状態|じょうたい}: an unarmed/defenseless state
- {丸腰|まるごし}で{立|た}ち{向|む}かう: to face something defenseless

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {素手|すで}: bare-handed — emphasizes using only one's hands, without tools or weapons
- {無防備|むぼうび}: defenseless; unguarded — emphasizes vulnerability and lack of defense
- {手ぶら}: empty-handed — refers to not carrying anything; often used casually for visiting without gifts
